title: WSLua DissectorTable GUID Support
description:
This merge request contains the functionality requested in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/19427

> Wireshark Lua currently only supports String and Integer types when adding a custom Lua dissector to a DissectorTable. This works fine for things like "tcp.port", but protocols extending from DCERPC need to hook the "dcerpc.uuid" table via GUIDs which is not currently supported.

This branch adds the functionality required for a Lua dissector to extend DCERPC via the "dcerpc.uuid" DissectorTable.

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12846/diffs?diff_id=830581615&start_sha=565c3d31117572f3fdb031d160208f8a2af147f4)

Even though we're unlikely to have a table name which starts with DCERPC_TABLE_NAME but has a suffix, isn't strcmp() more technically correct here instead of strncmp? 

And actually, could you add a comment explaining what this if-test is doing? My 30-second read of it didn't make it obvious to me. :smile:
Will do.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12846/diffs?diff_id=832791480&start_sha=094483eea5f156da842fd4991acd2f8c07d2aa46#23f725c3c477eb8e1461df65dcb821f2c1b06c9e_414_414)

Can you combine this with dceprc_init_uuid so there's less code duplication? Could dcerpc_init_uuid() call create_dissector_handle to get the guid_handle, and then just calls function? Something along those lines?

This one is a bit trickier since wslua_dissector.c only offers the existing dissector handle whereas the dcerpc_init_uuid is building the handle from pieces and registering individual procedures. Trying with create_dissector_handle led to downstream issues since the Lua dissector is mostly self-contained whereas builtin and plugin dissectors are somewhat more expressive. (for example, packet-dcerpc-initshutdown.c:534)

I'm hesitant to add the handle field to the existing dcerpc_init_uuid function since it might add a level of ambiguity to its intent (and would require modifying every location that uses it).

Would it be acceptable to instead extract the duplicate code from dcerpc_init_uuid and dcerpc_init_from_handle and have them call into that once they've completed their case-specific tasks?

Sure. I just wanted to avoid having 2 copies of code with some tricky steps in it, in case we needed to modify those steps in the future.  If you find a good way to do this, then great, even if it's partial. If the result is too cumbersome or awkward, then we can ignore my comment entirely.
I'm no expert in the wmem_tree_* API, but why use the _array version of the function when you really only have 1 guidkey, and the 2nd guidkey is NULL?
assigned to @gilramir
